answer: Finite-field phase space, a finite mode cutoff, finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space, and foundational finitism change different mathematical axes. A fixed F_q phase space replaces classical phase-space coordinates by finite-field elements but the associated quantum carrier in the cited construction is still q-dimensional over C. A Weyl energy cutoff keeps real/complex scalars and retains only finitely many coordinates from an explicitly countable tower. Finite Hilbert dimension restricts vector dimension without making the scalar continuum finite. Finitism rejects or recodes actual infinity and is not obtained merely by using a regulator. No equivalence or continuum bridge among these objects is supplied by either construction.

typed_objects.size: q^2 points, q(q+1) affine lines, q+1 striations

typed_objects.quantum_carrier: finite-dimensional subspace of an explicitly countable l2 completion
typed_objects.infinity_status: regulator value finite; parent tower countably infinite
typed_objects.physical_role: spectral truncation of continuum-field reduced modes

typed_objects.scalar_axis: uncountable complex scalar structure in ordinary foundations
typed_objects.infinity_status: finite basis does not remove infinite scalar sets

typed_objects.carrier: foundation admitting only finite objects or potential-infinity codes
typed_objects.scalar_axis: requires a separate construction of number/approximation objects
typed_objects.quantum_carrier: must be reformulated within the chosen finite foundation
typed_objects.physical_role: change of background mathematics, not a discretization by itself

pairwise_non_equivalence.witness: different scalar coordinate fields and different meaning of finiteness; q labels a field/state dimension while N bounds energy
the cited finite-field construction uses both F_q^2 and C^q; they are not the same carrier
a cutoff is an inclusion into a specified countable parent with convergence obligations; an abstract C^d has no such parent map
a finite regulator inside ZF/ZFC does not reject actual infinity or construct a finitist continuum replacement
one finite model at fixed q does not supply a foundation, a family principle, or a continuum-limit interpretation
ordinary C^d still quantifies over complex numbers and functions unless separately recoded

finite_field_to_continuum: a directed family of q values or another refinement parameter
embeddings/coarse-graining maps between noncanonically related finite fields
finite_math_to_physics: finite coding of scalars and probabilities
proof that the target laws survive the reformulation

literature_dependency.boundary: The source establishes finite-field discrete phase space for prime-power quantum dimensions; the comparison with Weyl mode cutoffs and finitism is this ledger's analysis.

does_not_establish: a no-go theorem for finite-field physics
a continuum limit of finite-field Wigner systems
a finitist construction of real or complex analysis
empirical evidence for or against actual infinity
a finite formulation of interacting Weyl gravity
next_gate: Any proposed bridge must select one pair of typed objects and supply explicit comparison maps plus a convergence or interpretation theorem; cardinality resemblance is not a bridge.
